question: Does a bounded current-density-conditioned marked topology remove P4CO's cross-source tail without target or source-identity access?
primary_basis: ITU-T H Supplement 21 (01/2025): light-dependent film-grain parameters
Ameur et al., FGA-NN, arXiv:2506.14350: analysis predicts conventional synthesis parameters
Newson et al., resolution-independent stochastic film grain: inhomogeneous Boolean intensity depends on image level

confirmation.selection_rule: Sort eligible first clips with ten PNG frames and select indices 24 through 27; confirmation pixels remain unread until both bin parameters and all model statistics freeze.

patch_observation.residual_normalization: subtract mean and divide by population RMS

candidate.name: two-bin-current-density-marked-phase-v1
candidate.construction: use only the current patch lowpass mean to select one of two globally fitted parent counts; generate the fixed signed clustered skeleton and project to exact Thomas power
candidate.fit_rule: independently minimize median patch feature distance in mean<0.5 and mean>=0.5 development bins; ties choose lower count
candidate.feature_distance: patchwise RMS feature distance scaled by fixed Gaussian-control MAD; aggregate by source median

branch_rule.pass: Retain current-density conditioning as a generic high-order development mechanism and open disjoint photographic severe-artifact stress.
branch_rule.fail: Close this exact split, counts and source roles without threshold, split or same-cohort rescue.

forbidden: read confirmation pixels before both bin counts and model statistics freeze
use source identity, target pixels, observed residual features or confirmation outcomes to choose a count
change split, grid, features or gates after development
claim stock, emulsion, scanner, process, physical calibration, visual safety or product readiness
claim_ceiling: Fresh-source archival current-density/grain-topology evidence only; no stock, calibration, scanner separation, visual safety or product claim.
